lines: Aftermath of the July Uprising At least 20 people are injured, several with spear wounds, in an armed clash between the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and the Awami League over local dominance and control of brick kilns in Fatullah, Narayanganj District, Bangladesh, with police firing rubber bullets and tear gas to disperse them. (The Daily Star)

2026 Iran war fuel crisis Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic Airways announces that its Norwegian operating subsidiary filed for bankruptcy after failing to secure short-term funding amid rising fuel costs, cancelling all flights and suspending ticket sales. (CNBC)

Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency terminates the search for 14 missing miners after flooding at an unauthorized gold mine in Bogor Regency, West Java, killed 13 people, citing risks of landslides and mine shaft collapses. (AFP)

Mexico–United States relations, Mexican drug war The Mexican government files a formal complaint with the United States regarding the anonymous tip lines set up by the Drug Enforcement Administration to receive information about members of organized crime and officials allegedly linked to them. (Reuters)

2026 New Zealand general election The counting of special votes results in the National Party losing two electorate seats, including one overhang seat. The National–ACT–NZ First coalition government falls below a majority to 65 seats, placing the Opportunity Party into a kingmaker position. (BBC News) (RNZ)

2026–27 ISU Grand Prix of Figure Skating 2026 NHK Trophy In figure skating, Ilia Malinin of the United States sets a men's short programme world record with 114.81 points at the NHK Trophy in Tokyo, Japan, surpassing compatriot Nathan Chen's previous record of 113.97 points set at the 2022 Winter Olympics. (AFP via France 24)
